Subject: Sales discovery: model fit & regression concerns

Hi James —

Thanks for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of discovery:
- Main goal: improve product summary relevance for category pages (higher precision on entity extraction + consistent tone)
- Current pain: after the vendor model v1.4.x update (Nov 10) you’ve seen a measurable drop in summary quality for 2 of 3 benchmark slices (longer descriptions, SKU-rich pages)
- Constraints: latency SLO ~150ms p95, cost target ~0.015 USD/token, must keep PII redaction intact

Redwood recommendations (initial):
1) Recommended models to evaluate: redwood/gpt-medium-quantized-v2 (good balance of cost & quality), open/llama-3-13b (higher quality for the problematic slices)
2) Prompt sets: attached prompt_set_v2.csv (contains the post-call prompt variants we discussed)
3) Eval links: I’ve uploaded our initial benchmark run here: https://redwood.ai/evals/acme-retail/2026-11-18 (contains per-slice metrics and sample outputs)

Immediate asks from Acme (per call):
- Provide a short diff summary between the previous model (v1.3.9) and the updated v1.4.x that could explain the change in behavior
- Pin or rollback options and timeline (we can support a temporary pin while we run deeper evals)
- If possible, a focused A/B evaluation with the recommended models plus your prod traffic sample set

I attached a short model_eval_report.pdf and the prompt set. I’ll loop in Rishi and Dev to scope the rollback/pinning path and commercial implications.

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa + Dev: confirm rollback/pin feasibility and timeline (ETA: 48 hours)
- Marissa + James: agree on 1–2 primary sample IDs for a focused assessment (James to confirm)
- Rishi: review commercial remediation options if rollback is needed

Thanks again — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0173

Hi all —

Quick technical summary after an initial pass on the supplied examples and our internal diffs: 

Findings (initial):
- The primary delta appears to be a beam-scoring parameter change and a small tokenizer normalization tweak introduced in v1.4.0 -> v1.4.x that affects longer, SKU-dense inputs (it compresses punctuation tokens differently leading to truncated context in some cases)
- We reproduced the behavior locally on a matching infra snapshot using your sample set (see diffs.zip)

Proposed remediation (low-risk path):
1) Pin project routing to v1.3.9 for Acme (this is a config-level change on our side; no infra re-deploy needed) — estimated completion: 4 hours after sign-off
2) Run a 24-hour A/B: v1.3.9 (pinned) vs redwood/gpt-medium-quantized-v2 to measure quality/latency/cost delta (we’ll surface per-slice metrics) — ETA for results: 48 hours after pin
3) If pinning is sufficient, we can keep v1.3.9 pinned while we iterate on a longer-term model recommendation

Artifacts we’ll produce: diff summary (text), reproduction notebook, pinned-config instructions (pin-instructions.txt) — attached diffs.zip contains early diffs and a short repro script.

Risks: the pinned variant will not include improvements from v1.4.x; if there are security or compliance fixes in v1.4.x we’ll need to patch them separately or backport. I’ll validate if any critical fixes must be applied before pinning.

Ask from Acme: please confirm you want us to proceed with pinning to v1.3.9 and provide the 5–10 sample IDs for the rapid manual check.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
